title: the proof reads a written name as the matcher does
line: a name an accepted record writes with a nickname, a spelling variant of the surname or a name the person is known by (an alias an accepted record gave) agrees in the written proof, in the matcher's own words; a name of another given name still says what it says

steps.say: the 1950 household: the son written Fred M Ahern, his wife Helen B Ahearn
the son accepted on the record

some.agrees: agrees: a given name a nickname or spelling variant

expect.why: Fred is a nickname of Frederick and M an initial of Micheal: the matcher takes both, so the proof says the record agrees, not that it says another name
no accepted statement of his name says another name than his

steps.say: his mother accepted on the record, written Helen B Ahearn: the surname she married into, which no name of hers carries

some.agrees: agrees: a name the person is known by

expect.why: the matcher reads the aliases a person holds as their names, so a name of her married life agrees; the note says it is an alias that holds it
no accepted statement of her name says another name than hers
